entries.title: Jeremiah 44:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: At Migdol - It seems the Jews that went into Egypt had planted themselves at these four places. Migdol was a city upon the borders of the Red Sea. Noph was a city, which the Greeks and Latines called Memphis; it is thought to be that, which is now called Cairo. Pathros was the province, since called Thebais.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For none - Only such shall escape, as have been forced into Egypt against their wills; and as did not fall in with the idolatry of the Egyptians.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: All the men - It should seem those that did it were mostly women, and that they did it with some privacy, so that all their husbands did not know of it.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The Lord liveth - There shall not any be left alive of the Jews that are in Egypt, to swear The Lord God liveth.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: This shall be a sign - Signs are usually antecedent to the thing signified, but the word is taken in a larger notion in this place for that which should attend the thing signified by it.
